Subject: Production: sudden p95/p99 regressions and 504s (started ~08:55 PT)

Connor —

We're seeing a sharp spike in p95/p99 for the /generate endpoint starting ~08:55 PT (today). A bunch of our user requests are getting 504s and the tail latency is up ~5-8x. This started right after our morning ingest job ramped and doesn't line up with our traffic (we're steady).

Quick facts from our side:

- p95 jumped to ~1.8s (from ~220ms)
- p99 jumped to ~6s (from ~420ms)

We've attached a short log export (acme_latency_logs_0822.txt) and a screenshot of our self-service dashboard. Can you confirm if this is a Redwood-side issue or something on our config? This is impacting several paid customers within our product.

Please escalate.

—Elaine

Thanks for the report, Elaine — we've started triage. Initial signals:
- We saw a correlated increase in long-running inference workers in a subset of the us-west region around 08:50 PT.
- Autoscaler did not provision additional warm workers quickly due to a recent change in the cooldown logic (INF-9123). That caused occasional queuing and timeouts under bursty backend KV cache misses.
- We're running a hotfix to adjust the cooldown threshold and force additional workers into service.

Interim mitigation applied:
- Forced scale-up of the affected pool at 10:04 PT (reduced 504s).
- Enabled a temporary request-routing rule to favor other healthy pools for Acme traffic.

Attachments: acme_latency_logs_0822.txt

I'll keep posting updates. We're treating this as an incident and will open INF-9123 for the root-cause work.

Markus Klein
Head of Inference Infrastructure, Redwood Inference

Subject: [Incident] Status update: degraded tail latency for /generate — Mitigation in place

Hi all —

Quick update for visibility: we've posted an incident on the public status page and are tracking the event under incident INC-20260822-01. Summary: tail latency (p95/p99) experienced a regression due to an autoscaler cooldown regression. Impact: elevated p95/p99 and a small percentage of 504s for customers routing to the affected pool.

What we did: forced a scale-up, applied temporary routing to healthy pools, and rolled a hotfix to the cooldown logic.

Customer-facing note: We will follow up with a post-incident analysis and recommended config changes to avoid similar impact. For Acme specifically, we're proposing a one-time goodwill credit for the affected window; Laura will share details.

Public incident link: https://status.redwoodinference.com/incidents/INC-20260822-01
Internal ticket: https://redwoodinference.atlassian.net/browse/INF-9123

Elaine / Acme team —

Thanks again for flagging this and for your patience while our teams worked through the incident. Below is a concise post-incident summary and proposed customer next steps:

Summary (what happened):
- Root cause: a recent change to autoscaler cooldown logic (INF-9123) delayed warm-worker provisioning under short burst conditions, which, combined with a small set of KV cache misses, produced higher queueing and 504s for requests routed to one pool.
- Timeline: issue began ~08:55 PT on 2026-08-22, mitigation (forced scale-up + routing) executed by 10:04 PT. Full rollback of the problematic cooldown param at 11:20 PT.

Customer impact and remediation:
- Impact window: ~1h10m (08:55–10:05 PT).
- Measured impact for Acme: elevated p95/p99 and ~0.6% 504 rate during window (we'll share token-level traces if desired).
- What we did for Acme: temporary routing to healthy pools during the incident, and issued a proposed one-time credit for the affected period (see attached sla-credits-proposal.docx).

Action items (owner / ETA):
- Engineering to complete INF-9123 permanent fix and add a test for cooldown regressions (Markus) / ETA: 2026-08-27
- Product Ops to add an automated alert for autoscaler lagging under KV miss spikes (Stephanie) / ETA: 2026-08-26
- AE to finalize goodwill credit and confirm with Acme (Laura) / ETA: 2026-08-24
- Connor to coordinate a technical review call with Acme if they want deeper traces / ETA: schedule within 48h

We appreciate the escalation — if you want a short exec-level note for your leadership we can prepare one. Please let us know if you need the token-level traces or additional logs.

Attachments: sla-credits-proposal.docx, acme_latency_logs_0822.txt

Regards,
Connor O'Brien
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
